name: brake_after_warning
description: RETUNED 2026-08-05 (second pass) from mdadas_run2's real telemetry. The first redesign reacted at t=3.1s, anchored to the CLOSED-FORM derived t_warn=3.0s -- but the companion scenario md_aeb_stationary_lead.xosc (same v_close=16.0/gap0=104.0m up to the point either scenario's driver reacts) measured the warning actually firing at t=3.30s (gt.fcw ACTIVE, frame 65), not 3.0s. That meant this profile's old onset (t=3.1) started braking BEFORE the warning existed, which pulled v_close down early enough that gt.fcw never even reached its own gate ('adas_state_matches' FAIL, 'no reported frame had gt.fcw.state_name == active'). This was not just a numeric miss -- the slug (md-fcw-warning-only-episode) means 'the driver reacted TO the warning', which structurally requires the reaction to start AFTER the warning is observed to fire, not after some earlier closed-form estimate of when it might. The lesson (recorded in md_fcw_warning_only.md): a reaction profile must be anchored to a MEASURED onset, not a derived one -- the closed form is good enough to design the approach geometry (it correctly predicted intervention would trip later than warning, with margin), but not precise enough to time a reaction against, because it does not model the ~0.4-0.5 m/s^2 coast-down (or other first-frame transients) that shifted the real crossing by 0.30s. Reaction now starts at t=3.5 (0.20s after the MEASURED t=3.30, comfortable margin against frame-to-frame variation), ramps to 0.6 by t=3.8. Measured intervention-if-unmanaged was t=4.75 in the companion run, so this leaves ~0.95s of margin before that reference point for the brake to take effect -- narrower than the first attempt's (unverified) 0.9s-against-a-derived-value, but now anchored to a real measurement. Level (0.6) unchanged from the first attempt; if this is still too weak the standing rule is to react earlier within [3.30,4.75] or brake harder, never touch the matcher.
